Course: "10. Tissues and Its Types" · subject: Science and Technology · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a plan_videos card:
- card.parts are the chapter's concepts (part_id = concept id) with their content type; card.coverage.must_cover lists every concept id,
  and each must be in the concept_ids of some video. card.context.map_slice has one row per concept: [concept id, type, pages, name].
- The source has the chapter summary, how the concepts link ([from, link, to]: pre = prerequisite, part, kind, cause, compare, seq =
  sequence, example, test), the prerequisites to teach, BIE's teaching order and the exam focus.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the chapter is about, the key questions the plan must serve, your main decisions with a
  reason each, what is uncertain.
- videos: in teaching order. First, when the source lists prerequisites, the "pehle yeh jaan lo" video: video_id "v0", kind
  "prerequisites", concept_ids [], prerequisites_taught = every prerequisite name exactly as given, estimated_minutes 5-8. Then the
  topic videos "v1", "v2" ...: kind "topic", prerequisites_taught [] (a topic video only reminds of a prerequisite, in at most 2 beats).
  title in the learner language; goal = what the student will understand after it; concept_ids = the concept ids taught in it, in
  order (every concept in some topic video); opening_hook = a real-life question, puzzle or surprise that opens it; story_or_analogy =
  the story or analogy that genuinely helps, or "" if none fits; estimated_minutes = within the video's narration budget: the sum of
  its concepts' minutes in the source (6-8 minutes per book page, S2-01); length_note = "" or, only for a very dense video, why it needs
  up to 25% more; why_this_unit = why these concepts belong together. Group concepts so that every topic video gets at least 3
  minutes (its hook, teaching and recap need room). All videos together stay within the chapter's minutes. A classification concept
  (a family: the types of a tissue, the kinds of a rock) is taught through the family pattern (the overview tree, every member in
  the same slots, the comparison, a memory trick), so keep a family and its members in one video where the time allows.
- chapter_flow: how the videos build on each other.
Reply with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

Chapter summary: Cells form tissues that divide work and build organs, organ systems and organisms. The chapter compares cell division, classifies animal and plant tissues, relates their microscopic structure to location and function, and tests recognition through diagrams, comparisons and multiple-choice questions.

Prerequisites to teach (name · needed for · basis · why):
- Cell boundaries, organelles and plant–animal cell differences · needed for c01, c02, c03, c05, c06, c07, c08, c09, c11, c12, c13, c14, c15, c16, c17, c18, c19, c20, c21, c22, c23, c24, c25, c26, c27, c28 · outside · Directly needed to distinguish nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane, wall, vacuole and chloroplast, and to interpret living contents, intercellular spaces, multinucleate fibres and extracellular material.
- Chromosomes, homologous pairs, chromatids, DNA replication and chromosome sets · needed for c02, c03 · outside · Directly needed for the eleven cell-division comparisons, including nuclear phases, ploidy, crossing over and correction of the chromosome-doubling claim.
- Somatic cells, germ cells, gametes and fertilisation · needed for c02 · outside · Directly needed to understand where mitosis and meiosis occur, what their products do and why chromosome-number reduction matters.
- Locations and roles of the named human organs, passages and skeleton · needed for c04, c05, c06, c07, c08, c10, c11, c13, c14, c15, c16, c17, c29, c33, c35 · outside · Directly needed for tissue-location lists: skin, gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts, lung air sacs, kidney tubules and urinary passages, glands and ducts, brain and spinal cord, heart, vessels, bones and joints.
- Plant organ landmarks and sections · needed for c03, c18, c19, c21, c22, c23, c24, c25, c27, c28, c30, c34 · outside · Directly needed to locate tissues using root and shoot tips, leaf base, node, internode, petiole, bark, vascular bundle, seed coverings, dicot and monocot, and the named stem regions.
- Diffusion, absorption, secretion and movement through walls or pores · needed for c06, c07, c09, c10, c25, c26, c27, c28, c34 · outside · Directly needed to interpret thin exchange surfaces, epithelial and gland functions, microvilli, tissue-fluid movement, permeability, wall pits, sieve plates and stomatal gas exchange.
- Photosynthesis, food storage and the functions of structural biological materials · needed for c07, c09, c10, c11, c12, c20, c21, c22, c23, c24, c25, c26, c28, c29, c31, c34 · outside · Directly needed to understand chlorophyll and food production, transport from leaves, fat as an energy reserve, and how proteins, polysaccharides, cellulose, lignin, keratin and suberin differ from tissues.
- Physical meanings of tension, elasticity, pressure, buoyancy and insulation · needed for c09, c10, c12, c13, c14, c15, c16, c19, c21, c22, c23, c24, c25, c28, c29, c31, c35 · outside · Directly needed to connect fibres with pulling and recoil, muscle contraction with movement or pumping, air spaces with floating, and subcutaneous fat with reduced heat loss; also distinguishes lengthwise growth from increased girth.
- Stimulus, nerve impulse, electrical signal and voluntary versus involuntary control · needed for c04, c13, c14, c15, c16, c17, c33 · outside · Directly needed to distinguish muscle-control categories and understand the neuron's directional signal diagram; these meanings cannot be inferred from shape or organ location alone.

BIE's teaching order: c01, c02, c03, c04, c05, c06, c07, c08, c09, c10, c11, c29, c12, c13, c14, c15, c16, c33, c35, c17, c18, c19, c30, c20, c21, c22, c23, c24, c31, c25, c26, c27, c28, c32, c34

Exam focus:
- c02: High-yield comparisons include division number, daughter-cell number, ploidy, crossing over and equational versus reduction division; the erroneous replication row needs explicit correction.
- c03: Cell plate versus cleavage, asters and centrioles, and meristem localisation are common plant–animal comparison criteria.
- c04: The four primary animal-tissue groups and connective subgroups support classification, matching and odd-one-out questions.
- c07: Epithelial shape–layer–location–function combinations are high-yield matching material, especially diffusion, protection, secretion and stretching.
- c08: Diagrams test recognition independently of memorised names, including apparent versus true stratification.
- c09: Matrix, collagen, elastic and reticular fibres distinguish connective tissue and explain mechanical properties.
- c10: Locations and functions of cartilage, bone, blood, adipose and dense connective tissue are directly examinable.
- c11: Haversian canals, canaliculi, chondrocytes, adipocytes and blood-cell labels are distinctive identification facts.
- c16: Three-way muscle comparison tests branching, striation, nuclei, control, location and function; cardiac muscle breaks the striated-equals-voluntary shortcut.
- c17: Neuron parts, synapse location and signal direction are central structure–function questions.
- c18: The complete plant-tissue hierarchy supports classification and component-based elimination.
- c19: Apical, lateral and intercalary locations and length-versus-girth effects are directly tested by a supplied statement question.
- c21: Chlorenchyma versus aerenchyma distinguishes photosynthesis from buoyancy and is directly tested.
- c24: Living versus dead cells, primary versus lignified secondary walls, spaces, contents, occurrence and support functions are core simple-tissue comparisons.
- c25: Four xylem components and their conduction, storage and support functions enable precise odd-one-out answers.
- c26: Phloem membership and the dead-fibre exception prevent misleading all-living generalisations.
- c28: Transported material, vascular arrangement and component-level exceptions are high-yield; printed oversimplifications must not become absolute exam rules.
- c29: The supplied HPAS 2020 PYQ directly tests subcutaneous fat as protection against heat loss.
- c33: The supplied cardiac statement question tests independent classification by appearance and control, with a continuation-wording warning.
- c34: Supplied questions test epidermis versus wall material and stomatal pore versus guard cells; explanations require clearly marked outside support.
- c35: Tendon versus ligament versus cartilage is a high-yield attachment and function distinction directly tested on the page.

videos.opening_hook: एक ही शरीर में skin ढकती है, muscle खींचता है और nerve message पहुँचाती है—इनको समझने से पहले cell में क्या पहचानना जरूरी है?
videos.story_or_analogy: छोटे visual examples: कमरे की boundary से membrane और wall का फर्क, खिंचे rubber से elasticity, पानी पर तैरती चीज से buoyancy और गरम कपड़े से insulation। हर analogy की सीमा बताई जाएगी; यह बाहर का standard textbook-level support है।
videos.why_this_unit: Cell sketch, chromosome-pair sketch, body–plant locator और everyday physical examples से हर prerequisite को meaning तथा example मिलेगा। Replication में DNA बढ़ने और chromosome sets बदलने को अलग समझाया जाएगा; organelles या reproduction का पूरा पुराना chapter नहीं खुलेगा।

videos.title: Cells मिलकर tissue कैसे बनाते हैं?
videos.goal: आप division of labour से tissue, organ, organ system और organism का रिश्ता समझेंगे; mitosis–meiosis तथा plant–animal mitosis को book के सभी comparison criteria पर अलग कर सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: चोट के बाद skin ठीक होती है, लेकिन बच्चे बनने की प्रक्रिया में chromosome number आधा करना क्यों जरूरी होता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: अलग काम करने वाली teams मिलकर एक काम पूरा करती हैं—इससे division of labour समझेंगे, फिर cell से organism तक असली biological levels पर लौटेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Organisation के बाद cells की संख्या और उनके बनने का तरीका स्वाभाविक अगला सवाल है। दोनों comparisons में common basis, हर criterion के दोनों पक्ष और recap table आएँगे; DNA replication को chromosome-number doubling समझने की गलती साफ अलग की जाएगी।

videos.title: Animal tissues: शरीर में कौन क्या करता है?
videos.goal: आप 4 primary animal-tissue groups और book में दिए connective subgroups का tree बना सकेंगे तथा body diagram में tissue, जगह और काम जोड़ सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: आपके हाथ की skin, उसके नीचे की चर्बी, muscle और nerve—क्या ये सब एक ही तरह का tissue हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: हाथ से शुरुआत करके body diagram में बाहर से अंदर जाएँगे: covering, जोड़ने-सहारा देने वाला material, movement और message।
videos.why_this_unit: Classification tree को human-body locator के साथ पढ़ने से नाम जगह और function से जुड़ेंगे। हर group के समान परिचय-slots, मुख्य फर्क और छोटा memory cue होगा; बाद के videos इन्हीं branches को खोलेंगे। Figure के हर label को तय reading path से पढ़ेंगे।

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: covering की बनावट काम कैसे बदलती है?
videos.goal: आप epithelial sheets, barriers और gland formation समझेंगे; book के हर epithelial type को layers, shape, special feature, location तथा function से पहचानेंगे और drawings में true तथा apparent stratification अलग करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Skin को बचाव करना है और lung air sacs को gases पार होने देनी हैं—क्या दोनों जगह एक जैसी covering चलेगी?
videos.story_or_analogy: पतली exchange boundary और कई layers वाले protective cover की तुलना केवल thickness–function link समझाने के लिए होगी; हर निष्कर्ष असली tissue और book के location पर लौटेगा।
videos.why_this_unit: Sheet की common structure के बाद पूरा epithelial family tree आएगा। हर member समान slots में खुलेगा, फिर उसका drawing और location zoom होगा। अंत में confused pairs, side-by-side comparison, memory cue और matching-style check होगा।

videos.title: Connective tissue: matrix से support, storage और transport तक
videos.goal: आप matrix और fibres से connective tissues के गुण समझेंगे; book की सभी varieties, locations तथा atlas labels पहचानेंगे और subcutaneous fat वाले HPAS 2020 question का कारण सहित उत्तर दे सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Blood बहता है और bone सख्त होती है—फिर दोनों connective tissue कैसे हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Cells के आसपास का material बदलने से tissue का व्यवहार बदलता है। खिंचाव और वापस लौटने के छोटे demonstrations collagen तथा elastic fibres का फर्क खोलेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Common matrix–fibre structure से varieties की properties निकलेंगी। Overview के बाद हर member की structure, नाम का आधार जहाँ book देता है, feature, function और location पढ़ेंगे। Atlas में Haversian canals, canaliculi, chondrocytes, adipocytes और blood-cell labels पहचानेंगे; अंत में fat से कम heat loss की cause chain और supplied PYQ करेंगे।

videos.title: Muscle और nerve: खिंचाव, control और message का रास्ता
videos.goal: आप contraction से movement का रिश्ता, skeletal–smooth–cardiac muscle का पूरा comparison, tendon attachment और neuron में impulse की direction समझेंगे; striation को voluntary control का प्रमाण नहीं मानेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: आप हाथ उठाना रोक सकते हैं, लेकिन heartbeat को उसी तरह रोकने का आदेश क्यों नहीं दे सकते?
videos.story_or_analogy: हाथ मोड़ने का familiar action contraction, bone और tendon को जोड़ेगा। Neuron के लिए message का रास्ता केवल direction समझाने का सहारा होगा, biological mechanism का विकल्प नहीं।
videos.why_this_unit: पहले contraction का result, जगह और book में दिया mechanism; फिर 3-member muscle tree और हर member के समान structure–location–function slots होंगे। Comparison में branching, striation, nuclei और control अलग criteria रहेंगे। Cardiac question तथा tendon–ligament–cartilage distinction के बाद अलग neuron भाग में parts, synapse और arrows का reading path होगा। हर भाग का recap और अंत में एक closing recap होगा।

videos.title: Plant tissues का पूरा family tree
videos.goal: आप book के पूरे plant-tissue hierarchy को division के आधार सहित पढ़ सकेंगे और हर branch तथा member की जगह पहचान सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पेड़ की बढ़ती नोक, मुलायम पत्ती और सख्त तना—इन अलग कामों को एक tissue map में कैसे रखेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक family tree में पहले बड़ी branches, फिर छोटी branches खोलेंगे; plant के familiar हिस्से हर branch का location anchor होंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Pages 1 और 8 के classification material को एक जगह जोड़ना जरूरी है। हर division का आधार, सभी named members, book में दिए distinguishing features, comparison और memory cue यहीं पढ़ेंगे। आगे के videos इसी tree की structures और mechanisms खोलेंगे, classification फिर से नहीं दोहराएँगे।

videos.title: Plant कहाँ बढ़ता है और cells specialised कैसे बनते हैं?
videos.goal: आप meristematic cells की features, apical–lateral–intercalary locations और length–girth effects समझेंगे; supplied statements हल करेंगे और differentiation से permanent tissue बनने की प्रक्रिया समझेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पौधे की ऊँचाई बढ़ना और तने का मोटा होना—क्या दोनों का growth point एक ही जगह होता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Plant sketch पर tip, base और side को अलग रंग से track करेंगे, ताकि location से growth effect निकले, केवल नाम याद न करना पड़े।
videos.why_this_unit: Meristem types को समान cell-feature, location और growth-effect slots में compare करेंगे। तुरंत supplied location question से गलत pairing जाँचेंगे। फिर dividing cell से specialised permanent tissue तक book की differentiation sequence, उसकी conditions और result पढ़ेंगे।

videos.title: Simple permanent tissues: storage, flexibility और strength
videos.goal: आप parenchyma और उसकी specialisations, collenchyma तथा sclerenchyma को structure से function तक समझेंगे; living contents, walls, spaces और locations पर compare करके buoyancy वाले questions हल करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: मुलायम plant part, बिना टूटे मुड़ने वाला हिस्सा और सख्त seed covering—इनमें support का तरीका अलग क्यों है?
videos.story_or_analogy: मुड़ते plant part और कठोर covering को साथ देखकर flexibility तथा rigidity का फर्क खोलेंगे। Air spaces से floating का छोटा visual aerenchyma समझाएगा।
videos.why_this_unit: Simple permanent tissue की पूरी family एक साथ रहेगी। Overview tree के बाद हर member के समान slots, chlorenchyma–aerenchyma का function difference, wall thickening से support की cause chains और सभी comparative drawings पढ़ेंगे। सबसे confused pairs, full comparison table, memory cue और supplied practice अंत में होंगे।

videos.title: Xylem और phloem: components से transport समझें
videos.goal: आप complex tissue का मतलब, xylem और phloem के सभी components, उनके काम, labelled drawings और stem arrangement समझेंगे; living–dead exceptions तथा non-xylem component question सही करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: जड़ों से पानी और पत्तियों से बना food बाकी plant तक पहुँचता है—क्या दोनों के लिए एक जैसी transport line होती है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Transport network का visual अलग materials और routes समझाने में मदद करेगा; storage तथा support करने वाले components को भी दिखाएँगे, ताकि हर component को केवल pipe न मानें।
videos.why_this_unit: Whole vascular bundle से components तक zoom करेंगे। Xylem और phloem members के समान structure–function slots, diagrams के सारे labels और stem में arrangement के बाद side-by-side comparison आएगा। Xylem parenchyma तथा phloem fibres जैसे exceptions स्पष्ट होंगे; printed transport shortcuts को absolute rules नहीं बनाएँगे।

videos.title: Plant की protective covering और gas exchange: questions खोलकर समझें
videos.goal: आप protective covering को wall material से और stomatal pore को guard cells से अलग कर सकेंगे; supplied questions के हर option को कारण देकर जाँच सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पत्ती की covering बचाव भी करती है और gases का आना-जाना भी होने देती है—यह दोनों काम साथ कैसे होते हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Covering में opening और उसे नियंत्रित करने वाले हिस्सों का visual इस्तेमाल करेंगे; pore और guard cells को एक ही चीज मानने की सीमा वहीं साफ होगी।
videos.why_this_unit: इन practice questions में नए explanatory links हैं, इसलिए इन्हें जल्दबाजी वाले final quiz में नहीं दबाएँगे। Plant से leaf covering और फिर pore–guard cells तक zoom, function से structure का रिश्ता और option-wise reasoning पढ़ेंगे। Book से बाहर जरूरी epidermis, wall-material या gas-exchange support को स्पष्ट रूप से बाहर का standard textbook explanation बताएँगे।

output.chapter_flow: पहले 8 मिनट में सीधे जरूरी tools सीखेंगे। फिर organisation और cell division से animal-tissue tree बनेगा; epithelial, connective तथा muscle families अपने figures और questions सहित खुलेंगी, और neuron message की direction जोड़ेगा। इसके बाद plant-tissue tree से meristems, differentiation, simple permanent tissues और vascular tissues तक जाएँगे। आखिरी video protective covering तथा gas-exchange questions को समझाकर chapter बंद करेगा। सभी 35 concepts शामिल हैं; topic narration 100 मिनट और prerequisite सहित कुल 108 मिनट है। Topic videos prerequisites को अधिकतम 2 reminder beats में याद दिलाएँगे, दोबारा नहीं पढ़ाएँगे।

notes.about: Review of the video lesson plan for Chapter 10 (Tissues and Its Types) covering 1 prerequisite video and 10 topic videos across 35 concepts for UPSC / State PCS learners in Hinglish.
key_questions: Does the lesson plan cover all 35 required concepts in BIE's exact teaching order and within the per-concept narration budgets?
Are all 9 prerequisite groups taught in the 5-8 minute prerequisite video without bloat?
Do the video teaching plans follow the required content-type teaching patterns, exam focus points, and natural spoken Hinglish style?

decisions.decision: Pass the lesson plan with no blocking issues.
decisions.reason: Every concept c01-c35 is covered in exact teaching order, all time budgets match the sum of concept minutes (total 100 topic minutes + 8 prerequisite minutes), content-type patterns are explicitly planned, and exam traps/corrections (mitosis/meiosis replication row, cardiac muscle control, vascular tissue exceptions) are properly addressed.

problems.problem: v5 packs 8 concepts (c12, c13, c14, c15, c16, c33, c35, c17) into a 16-minute video, combining the entire muscle family, two practice concepts, and neuron impulse transmission.
problems.fix: Ensure during scriptwriting that the transition from tendon/bone attachment (c35) to neuron structure and impulse transmission (c17) is clearly signposted so c17 gets its full 1.7-2.3 minute process pattern without feeling rushed at the end of the muscle video.

checklist.note: Outside knowledge (9 prerequisites, replication row correction, epidermis/stomata explanations in c34) is explicitly marked as standard textbook support.
The plan integrates structures, classification trees, figures, comparisons, and PYQ/practice questions with deep conceptual links appropriate for UPSC/State PCS.
Notes clearly state what the unit is about, key teaching questions, main structural decisions with reasons, and uncertainties regarding missing page images.
Titles, goals, hooks, and notes are written in natural, clear teacher Hinglish (Devanagari Hindi with Roman English technical terms).
All 35 concepts (c01 to c35) and all 9 prerequisite groups are accounted for without cutting or merging away book items.
Each video plan specifies how concepts will be opened with hooks, visual analogies, cause-effect chains, and structure-function links.
Depth matches UPSC/State PCS requirements, explicitly targeting high-yield matching, statement traps, exceptions (like phloem fibres, xylem parenchyma, cardiac muscle), and diagram recognition.

Starts with one 8-minute prerequisite video (within 5-8 min), follows BIE's exact teaching order across v1-v10, and keeps every topic video within the sum of its concept budgets (total 100 minutes, well within the 84-112 minute chapter budget).

The progression from cell division to animal tissues (overview, epithelial, connective, muscle, nervous) and then plant tissues (overview, meristem, simple, complex, protective) flows logically and integrates practice questions right where their concepts are taught.
All 9 prerequisite groups are listed and planned in v0, and chapter_flow explicitly commits to reminding prerequisites in at most 2 beats in topic videos without re-teaching.
Uses Navin's mixed script (Hindi in Devanagari, English terms in Roman) with clean, conversational sentences.
Every concept_id claim in v1-v10 matches the goal and why_this_unit descriptions.

Each video's why_this_unit outlines the required content-type teaching patterns (structure zoom, comparison criteria and tables, classification trees and identical member slots, figure reading paths, cause-effect chains, and process steps).
Plans explicitly ensure identical slots for family members, explicit limits on analogies, and no duplicate recaps across videos.
